# VOID_AUDIT.md — Group 16 · Channel 0 (M2)

> **Engine**: VOIDBASTARD-TAO (Operational Emptiness Engine)
> **Scope**: `projects/g16/m2/`
> **Core Thesis**: *"One remote, one button. Every channel tells you the same thing: keep watching. The only real choice is whether to put the remote down."*

---

## 0. HONEST VIDEO-VS-GAME CRITIQUE & GEMINI PROVENANCE

### A. Brutally Honest Critique of Previous M2 Build vs. Omni 1.2 Flash Seed Video (`study/sheet.jpg` & `pairs/pair_*.jpg`)

1. **Tacky Non-Diegetic HUD Instruction Bar & Web2 Modal Boxes (`pair_002`, `pair_005`, `pair_008` right vs. left)**
   - **Before**: A literal floating debug-style instruction bar (`[SPACE / CLICK] FLIP CHANNEL     [P] PUT REMOTE DOWN`) sat plastered over the dark wooden table in the bottom-left corner of every frame. Worse, non-autostart entry and both endings (`TAKEN OVER` and `REMOTE SET DOWN`) dropped large rectangular Web2 modal boxes over the television, complete with gamey stat readouts (`SIGNAL COVERAGE: 100%`) and a parenthetical moralizing explanation: `(Putting the remote down was the one real choice.)`.
   - **Omni Video Truth**: Zero HUD text, zero floating banners, zero modal popups. The entire psychological horror relies on unmediated first-person presence: only the dim charcoal-sketched bedroom, the curved CRT glass with its stark monospace broadcast OSD (`CH 07` / `"you can stop thinking now"`), the physical remote held in the lower-right corner, and the encroaching `#ff00dc` / `#000000` missing-texture rot.

2. **Flat Vector Cartoon "Football Eye" on `CH 03` (`pair_005.00.jpg` right vs. left)**
   - **Before**: On `CH 03` (`"IT IS WATCHING"`), `drawWatchingEye()` pasted a smooth radial-gradient white vector almond over the bottom of the stairwell while leaving a harsh black doorway rectangle directly above it. Against the gritty chicken-scratch charcoal stairwell sprite, it looked like clean Flash clip-art pasted on top of an etching.
   - **Omni Video Truth (`f_022.jpg` / `f_023.jpg`)**: A massive, uncanny charcoal-shaded eyeball rises organically out of the stairwell void—complete with a curved, densely hatched graphite upper brow dome filling the doorway arch, a heavy cast shadow under the upper lid across the sclera and iris, hand-inked radial iris striations, and dark crosshatched under-eye creases resting onto the stair treads.

3. **Premature Wallpaper Corruption Dump & Missing Analog CRT Sync-Roll Tear (`pair_002.00.jpg` right vs. left)**
   - **Before**: Because `room_background_around_the_tv.png` was generated from mid-game study frames (`f_014.jpg`, `f_027.jpg`), it already had large pink/black checker clusters baked onto the wallpaper and right TV control panel. On `flips === 1`, the old code blended `assets.room` at `0.72` alpha immediately and spawned 6 extra clusters, jumping instantly from `0%` to `~80%` wallpaper corruption at `t = 2.0s` while leaving leftover black square smudges on `cleanRoomCanvas` and leaking a `19px` vertical strip on the right inner CRT edge (`SCR.w = 438` vs actual `444+`). Meanwhile, channel flips only drew faint horizontal grey bars instead of real horizontal sync-loss.
   - **Omni Video Truth (`f_001` -> `f_009` -> `f_012`)**: At `t = 0..1.8s` (`CH 07`), the bedroom is **100% uncorrupted**—only a tiny 7-block diagonal `#ff00dc`/`#000000` tear floats inside the CRT screen. When the thumb clicks to `CH 01` at `t = 2.0s` (`f_009.jpg`), the bedroom wallpaper is *still* clean while the CRT tube snaps into **wavy analog VHS/CRT horizontal sync-roll ribbons, right-edge white sync-curl sawtooths, and a thick dark rolling V-blank sync bar**, followed `0.25s` later (`f_010`..`f_012`) by missing-texture blocks erupting outward from the bezel seam.

4. **Missing `t = 8.0s` `SYSTEM ERROR` Screen Consumption & Cutout Fringe Halo (`pair_008.00.jpg` right vs. left)**
   - **Before**: At `t = 8.0s`, the old build sat on a tame `CH 02` corridor with scattered translucent rectangles, weak un-bloomed purple lines behind the TV, and a bright beige hand sporting a visible `[157, 157, 154]` light-grey cutout fringe halo from its `#d8d8d8` studio background.
   - **Omni Video Truth (`f_033.jpg`)**: By `t = 8.0s`, the camera pushes claustrophobically closer (`~1.13x`), the entire curved CRT tube fractures into a dense, horizontally-sheared `#ff00dc` & `#000000` missing-texture checkerboard (`"SYSTEM ERROR"`) with a static tear band across the middle, perspective checker patches spill onto the wooden tabletop, luminous neon-magenta (`#ff2ae5`) orthogonal wireframe tendrils crawl up both walls, and the player's hand/remote darkens into a nocturnal backlit silhouette rimmed in glowing neon magenta.

5. **Spoiled / Inaccessible Put-Down-Remote Discovery**
   - **Before**: Putting the remote down was spoiled on frame 1 by `[P] PUT REMOTE DOWN` HUD text, while the untouched stillness timer was set to `11.0s` and explicitly disabled under `?autostart`, preventing the stillness resolution from ever manifesting naturally in verification or short sessions.

### B. Honest Remaining Differences After Rebuild
Even after eliminating HUD/modal clutter, de-fringing sprites, restoring spotless wallpaper inpainting, synthesizing a 2-frame boiling charcoal-crosshatched eye, adding scanline-sheared CRT sync-roll + `SYSTEM ERROR` checker takeover, and choreographing untouched stillness into `CH 00`:
- **Neural Frame Morphing vs. Real-Time Sprite + Procedural Compositing**: `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` continuously hallucinates subtle 3D foreshortening changes across the hand's fingers and organic perspective-warped 3D checker cubes extruding out of the CRT glass (`f_040.jpg`), whereas our live 60fps HTML5 Canvas engine composites de-fringed `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` 2D plates (`room_background_around_the_tv.png`, `tv_frame_and_remote.png`, `8_channel_loops_still_or_2_frame.png`) with 2D affine tabletop shear, barrel-curved CRT Bézier clipping, and procedural orthogonal wireframe tendrils.
- **Playable 8-Channel Breadth + Stillness Arc**: The 10s Omni clip only visits `CH 07 -> CH 01 -> CH 03 -> SYSTEM ERROR` and ends in consumption; the live game supports all 8 distinct horror channels (`CH 01`–`CH 08`, direct tuning `1`–`8`, bidirectional flipping) PLUS the interactive spatial/untouched stillness arc into `CH 00` and `[R]` degauss recovery.

## 1. WAY

Channel 0 is a game about **compulsion as a single physical gesture**. You sit in a dark charcoal-drawn bedroom holding a plastic remote pointed at an analog CRT television. Every channel tells you to rely on the broadcast (`"you can stop thinking now"`, `"DO NOT LOOK BACK"`, `"IT IS WATCHING"`, `"WE ALREADY DECIDED FOR YOU"`), while every click tears another piece out of the room's reality—replacing bedroom wallpaper and wood grain with `#ff00dc` / `#000000` Half-Life 2 missing-texture checkerboards and glowing neon-magenta circuit veins.

The Way of the surface is **absolute first-person silence and diegetic truth**:
- The screen shows **only** the room, the curved CRT phosphor glass, the hand holding the remote, and the physical consequences of flipping vs. stillness.
- Interaction lives spatially **on the TV and the remote in your hand**: clicking the upper keypad/screen feeds the broadcast; clicking the lower grip/wrist—or simply **leaving the remote untouched for ~4.5 seconds**—lowers your hand, retracts the magenta rot back into the bezel, and clears the tube to `CH 00`.

---

## 2. OBSTRUCTION

What obstructed the player's direct contact with the work in the first-pass M2 build:
1. **Instructional Spoiler Chrome**: `[SPACE / CLICK] FLIP CHANNEL   [P] PUT REMOTE DOWN` turned an eerie existential realization—*that you can stop pressing the button*—into a mundane keybinding checklist on frame 1.
2. **Post-Mortem Modal Essay Boxes**: `renderTitleOverlay()` (`START`, `HOW TO PLAY [H]`) and `renderEndingOverlay()` (`TAKEN OVER`, `SIGNAL COVERAGE: 100%`, `(Putting the remote down was the one real choice.)`) broke spatial immersion by explaining the theme in a grey box instead of letting the room itself become consumed or healed.
3. **Visual Dishonesty on Key Channels**: A vector clip-art oval eye on `CH 03`, grey studio cutout fringes around the hand, missing horizontal CRT sync-roll on channel switches, and dumping `72%` of the baked room corruption on the very first click destroyed the gradual dread curve of the Omni seed video.

---

## 3. KEEP-CUT LEDGER

## 6. VOID CONTRACT

1. **Law 1 (Begin Empty)**: No floating HUD, score counters, keybind legends, or tutorial boxes exist anywhere in the DOM or Canvas.
2. **Law 2 (Present Operation Only)**: Only the room, the active CRT broadcast, and the physical remote in hand are rendered during play.
3. **Law 3 (One State = One Dominant Purpose)**: Flipping feeds the signal; stillness starves it.
4. **Law 4 (Display Actions Only While Valid)**: `[ POWER ]` phosphor appears only in `REST`; `[R] DEGAUSS` phosphor appears inside the CRT OSD **only** during `FAULT` (`flips >= 10` + `0.5s` settle).
5. **Law 5 (Spatial Controls Beside What They Change)**: Clicking the CRT or upper remote keypad depresses the button and flips channels; hovering/clicking the lower remote grip/wrist physically eases the hand downward to put the remote down.
6. **Law 6 (World Consequence Over Banners)**: Both endings (`COMPLETE` stillness on `CH 00` and `FAULT` `SYSTEM ERROR` consumption) transform the bedroom, lighting, zoom, and CRT tube directly—zero modal banners.
7. **Law 7 & 12 (Interruptibility & Quiet Completion)**: At any moment before `FAULT`, ceasing input for `4.5s` (or clicking the wrist / pressing `P`) halts corruption, retracts tendrils into the bezel, and settles on `CH 00` without nagging the player to restart.
8. **Law 8 & 14 (Recovery & Accessibility)**: Full keyboard parity (`Space`/`Enter`/`Arrows`/`1-8` flip, `P`/`Esc`/`ArrowDown`-hold lower, `R` degauss recovery) and clean `[R] DEGAUSS` recovery from `FAULT`.
9. **Law 11 (Motion Reports Real Change)**: Every CRT sync-tear, remote thumb depression, subtle `2.45s..4.5s` stillness hand-drop, and tendril retraction directly reflects underlying state variables (`syncTear`, `remoteClickAnim`, `remoteDropAnim`, `visualCorruption`).
10. **Law 13 (Empty Regions Inactive)**: Clicking empty bedroom walls outside the TV cabinet and physical remote triggers nothing and shows `cursor: default`.

---

## 7. FAILURE

- **Compulsive Over-Flipping (`FAULT`)**: Flipping 10 times drives `corruption` to `1.0`. Rather than punishing the player with a "GAME OVER" dialog box, the CRT locks into writhing, scanline-sheared `#ff00dc`/`#000000` missing-texture checkerboards (`"SYSTEM ERROR"`), zoomed claustrophobically close while the hand is swallowed in dark magenta-rimmed shadow. After `0.5s`, the CRT's bottom OSD line flickers `[R] DEGAUSS`, enabling a hardware cathode-collapse reset (`RECOVERY -> READY`).
- **Headless / Autoplay Audio Lock**: `bgm_loop.mp3` and `AudioContext` wrap `.play()` and `.resume()` in promise guards and unlock cleanly on the first keyboard or pointer event without throwing console errors.
- **Asset Load Sequencing**: Offscreen processing (`cleanRoomCanvas`, `cleanHandCanvas`, `darkHandCanvas`, `eyeFrames`) gates on `assets.readyCount === 3` with graceful fallback drawing if inspected mid-load.

---

## 8. IMPLEMENTATION

### Rebuilt Files

void_audit_sections.heading: 1. WAY
void_audit_sections.content:
Channel 0 is a game about **compulsion as a single physical gesture**. You sit in a dark charcoal-drawn bedroom holding a plastic remote pointed at an analog CRT television. Every channel tells you to rely on the broadcast (`"you can stop thinking now"`, `"DO NOT LOOK BACK"`, `"IT IS WATCHING"`, `"WE ALREADY DECIDED FOR YOU"`), while every click tears another piece out of the room's reality—replacing bedroom wallpaper and wood grain with `#ff00dc` / `#000000` Half-Life 2 missing-texture checkerboards and glowing neon-magenta circuit veins.

The Way of the surface is **absolute first-person silence and diegetic truth**:
- The screen shows **only** the room, the curved CRT phosphor glass, the hand holding the remote, and the physical consequences of flipping vs. stillness.
- Interaction lives spatially **on the TV and the remote in your hand**: clicking the upper keypad/screen feeds the broadcast; clicking the lower grip/wrist—or simply **leaving the remote untouched for ~4.5 seconds**—lowers your hand, retracts the magenta rot back into the bezel, and clears the tube to `CH 00`.

---

void_audit_sections.heading: 2. OBSTRUCTION
void_audit_sections.content:
What obstructed the player's direct contact with the work in the first-pass M2 build:
1. **Instructional Spoiler Chrome**: `[SPACE / CLICK] FLIP CHANNEL   [P] PUT REMOTE DOWN` turned an eerie existential realization—*that you can stop pressing the button*—into a mundane keybinding checklist on frame 1.
2. **Post-Mortem Modal Essay Boxes**: `renderTitleOverlay()` (`START`, `HOW TO PLAY [H]`) and `renderEndingOverlay()` (`TAKEN OVER`, `SIGNAL COVERAGE: 100%`, `(Putting the remote down was the one real choice.)`) broke spatial immersion by explaining the theme in a grey box instead of letting the room itself become consumed or healed.
3. **Visual Dishonesty on Key Channels**: A vector clip-art oval eye on `CH 03`, grey studio cutout fringes around the hand, missing horizontal CRT sync-roll on channel switches, and dumping `72%` of the baked room corruption on the very first click destroyed the gradual dread curve of the Omni seed video.

void_audit_sections.heading: A. `READY` (`CH 07` — Spotless Bedroom, Center Open, Spatial Zones Only)
C. `COMPLETE` (`CH 00` — Remote Lowered via ~4.5s Stillness or Wrist Click)
6. VOID CONTRACT
void_audit_sections.content:
1. **Law 1 (Begin Empty)**: No floating HUD, score counters, keybind legends, or tutorial boxes exist anywhere in the DOM or Canvas.
2. **Law 2 (Present Operation Only)**: Only the room, the active CRT broadcast, and the physical remote in hand are rendered during play.
3. **Law 3 (One State = One Dominant Purpose)**: Flipping feeds the signal; stillness starves it.
4. **Law 4 (Display Actions Only While Valid)**: `[ POWER ]` phosphor appears only in `REST`; `[R] DEGAUSS` phosphor appears inside the CRT OSD **only** during `FAULT` (`flips >= 10` + `0.5s` settle).
5. **Law 5 (Spatial Controls Beside What They Change)**: Clicking the CRT or upper remote keypad depresses the button and flips channels; hovering/clicking the lower remote grip/wrist physically eases the hand downward to put the remote down.
6. **Law 6 (World Consequence Over Banners)**: Both endings (`COMPLETE` stillness on `CH 00` and `FAULT` `SYSTEM ERROR` consumption) transform the bedroom, lighting, zoom, and CRT tube directly—zero modal banners.
7. **Law 7 & 12 (Interruptibility & Quiet Completion)**: At any moment before `FAULT`, ceasing input for `4.5s` (or clicking the wrist / pressing `P`) halts corruption, retracts tendrils into the bezel, and settles on `CH 00` without nagging the player to restart.
8. **Law 8 & 14 (Recovery & Accessibility)**: Full keyboard parity (`Space`/`Enter`/`Arrows`/`1-8` flip, `P`/`Esc`/`ArrowDown`-hold lower, `R` degauss recovery) and clean `[R] DEGAUSS` recovery from `FAULT`.
9. **Law 11 (Motion Reports Real Change)**: Every CRT sync-tear, remote thumb depression, subtle `2.45s..4.5s` stillness hand-drop, and tendril retraction directly reflects underlying state variables (`syncTear`, `remoteClickAnim`, `remoteDropAnim`, `visualCorruption`).
10. **Law 13 (Empty Regions Inactive)**: Clicking empty bedroom walls outside the TV cabinet and physical remote triggers nothing and shows `cursor: default`.

---

void_audit_sections.heading: 7. FAILURE
void_audit_sections.content:
- **Compulsive Over-Flipping (`FAULT`)**: Flipping 10 times drives `corruption` to `1.0`. Rather than punishing the player with a "GAME OVER" dialog box, the CRT locks into writhing, scanline-sheared `#ff00dc`/`#000000` missing-texture checkerboards (`"SYSTEM ERROR"`), zoomed claustrophobically close while the hand is swallowed in dark magenta-rimmed shadow. After `0.5s`, the CRT's bottom OSD line flickers `[R] DEGAUSS`, enabling a hardware cathode-collapse reset (`RECOVERY -> READY`).
- **Headless / Autoplay Audio Lock**: `bgm_loop.mp3` and `AudioContext` wrap `.play()` and `.resume()` in promise guards and unlock cleanly on the first keyboard or pointer event without throwing console errors.
- **Asset Load Sequencing**: Offscreen processing (`cleanRoomCanvas`, `cleanHandCanvas`, `darkHandCanvas`, `eyeFrames`) gates on `assets.readyCount === 3` with graceful fallback drawing if inspected mid-load.

# VOIDBASTARD-TAO AUDIT — `g18` · Capacity Crisis (M2)

> **VOIDBASTARD-TAO ONLINE. SHOW ONLY WHAT IS TRUE NOW.**
> Every visible element is a claim about what matters now. Removal is commitment: fewer true claims create a stronger surface.

---

## 0. HONEST VIDEO-VS-GAME CRITIQUE & GEMINI PROVENANCE

### A. Brutally Honest Before-Rebuild Critique (`pair_002`, `pair_005`, `pair_008` Before)
Comparing the first-pass `projects/g18/m2/game/index.html` side-by-side against the Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash seed video (`video/gameplay.mp4` / `study/sheet.jpg`) exposed five severe visual and systemic failures:

1. **Ugly Pasted Chip Cutouts with Circular Blue Fog Halos (`pair_002/005/008` right vs. left)**:
   - In the Omni video (`f_001` → `f_014` → `f_033`), the 4 foreground brown dirt lots clear into flush, nocturnal dark-slate architectural server-hall / cryo-heatsink modules (`#1c2530` fin valleys, `#5e748b` matte gunmetal silicon dies) whose circuit traces ignite strictly along the isometric pad trenches in electric cyan (`#38d8ff`) and golden-amber (`#ffb830`).
   - The first-pass game extracted studio-lit `#e5ebf0` bright white-silver sprites from `server_hall_and_chip_icons.png` without nocturnal color grading and drew `ctx.ellipse` radial blue gradients (`rgba(80,205,255,0.65)`) beneath every pad—turning the 4 server halls into bright floating stickers inside giant circular blue soap bubbles, while unbuilt lots stamped permanent `+ CHIP LOT` text labels over visible cyan bleed from the raw map asset.
2. **Uncleaned 3-Strip Composite Artifacts & Frozen Ghost Steam in `town_map_with_lights_3_load_levels.png`**:
   - Because `town_map_with_lights_3_load_levels.png` (`1376×768`) was generated as 3 vertical load-level strips (`x≈341` and `x≈687`), its right strip baked a **permanent static white mushroom cloud of steam** above the cooling towers (`x=765..912, y=0..265`) and pre-baked glowing pads in the foreground. In `pair_002` (`t=2s`), the Omni video has **zero steam** on its matte dark cooling towers while load is calm (`+12%`), whereas the old game showed a huge frozen painted cloud with moving circles layered over it.
3. **Detached Toast Banner Violating Law 6 (`drawMapToast`)**:
   - A 590px yellow-bordered toast box (`CHIP INSTALLED: Query cost -$0.01 -> Orders accelerating!` / `JEVONS REBOUND...`) sat pinned across the top-left transmission corridor—narrating in prose what the world's surging cables, boiling cooling towers, and flickering house windows were supposed to show physically.
4. **Severe Right-Sidebar Clutter (`drawDashboard`)**:
   - `sheet.jpg` has an iconic, monumental WarGames right panel (`x=912..1280`): **only** the 4 bold monospace bars (`MONEY`, `WATER`, `OPINION`, `DEMAND`), generous dark `#0d1114` void, and the stark bordered `WEEK 7 REQUEST` box (`+1 hall: clear 4 lots` → two-tone amber/green `+1 hall: COMPLETE`).
   - The first-pass build crammed in a top `DAY X/7 · ... $0.019/q` micro-header, a `112px` `GRID LOAD` sparkline box in the middle void, and 2–3 stacked verbose instruction buttons (`[SPACE] INSTALL GEN-3 PHOTON DIE`, `[1] SELL CAPACITY +$$$ · Jevons surge!`, etc.) inside the `WEEK 7` box—shrinking and crowding every element.
5. **Turn-Locked Menu Play & Opaque End Modals**:
   - Every 1.05s the simulation froze into a sidebar button-clicking prompt instead of letting Jevons' paradox play out spatially on the isometric grid, and `BLACKOUT` slapped a `690×360` opaque modal over the map—hiding the darkened miniature town at the exact moment its blackout mattered most.

### B. Honest Post-Rebuild Assessment & Remaining Differences
- **What Now Matches `sheet.jpg` & Exceeds First-Pass Playability**:
  - **Zero circular blue halos & nocturnal-graded flush modules**: Sprites extracted from `server_hall_and_chip_icons.png` are pixel-graded from `#d8d8d8` studio lighting down to nocturnal gunmetal slate (`#5e748b` / `#17212b`), seated on flush stepped isometric plinths, with 24 crisp isometric circuit conduits per pad pulsing in cyan (`#38d8ff`) and amber (`#ffb830`) strictly inside the pad geometry.
  - **Clean nocturnal base map & true zero-to-billowing steam**: Baked ghost steam above the hyperbolic cooling towers (`y < 263`), vertical strip dividers, and pre-baked foreground pad bleed are scrubbed offscreen; cooling towers stand crisp and silent at `t=0..2s` and billow volumetric steam only as halls boil cooling water.
  - **Stark `sheet.jpg` right panel**: Top micro-header, middle sparkline box, toast banner, and stacked sidebar buttons are 100% cut. Only `MONEY`, `WATER`, `OPINION`, `DEMAND`, and the exact `WEEK 7 REQUEST` box remain.
  - **Spatial Law-5 controls**: Clicking the 4 dirt lots / halls installs & upgrades dies directly in-world; 3 compact diegetic substation breaker switches (`[1] SELL`, `[2] BUFFER`, `[3] CAP`) sit right beside the substation transformers (`x=768, y=548..644`) with a live power filament routing into the Hall Bus, Battery Racks, or Town Limiter.
- **Remaining Honest Differences vs. Seed Video**:
  1. **Diegetic Substation Breaker Rack (`x=768..896, y=548..644`)**: The passive Omni video has no allocation switches visible because the video viewer cannot toggle `[1] SELL / [2] BUFFER / [3] CAP`; we place a compact 3-throw breaker unit in the empty lower-right substation corner (dormant at `t=0` when `0` halls are built, armed once compute is online) so the core verb (`Allocate: sell, save or cap`) is playable spatially without polluting the right panel.
  2. **Pad Drop-In Trajectory**: In `f_009`–`f_014` of the Omni video, Omni briefly hallucinates an upper-row chip silhouette translating across the town edge before settling onto the 4 foreground lots; in our playable build, clicking each of the 4 brown dirt lots drops its module cleanly (`32px` vertical cubic ease-out latch) onto that exact lot's coordinates so spatial mouse picking is 1:1 deterministic.
  3. **Procedural Canvas Plasma vs. Diffusion Lightning**: Our surging golden transmission filaments and pad-to-pad arcs use multi-strand procedural jittered polylines (`#ffb830` outer glow + `#fff4c8` core) rather than neural video diffusion blur, trading painterly softness for 60 fps real-time responsiveness to player breaker throws.

## 1. WAY
One miniature town shares one high-voltage substation with your expanding data center; every silicon efficiency upgrade cuts cost-per-query and immediately triggers a Jevons demand rebound across the overhead amber grid, forcing you to physically route substation power (`SELL`, `BUFFER`, `CAP`) beside the transformers to survive 7 days without plunging the neighborhood into blackout.

## 6. VOID CONTRACT
1. **Zero Floating Toasts**: No text banner may ever appear over the sky, transmission pylons, town roofs, or server pads to narrate system changes.
2. **Zero Circular Sprite Halos**: Server halls sit on flush isometric plinths (`#121a22`); all cyan (`#38d8ff`) and amber (`#ffb830`) illumination must follow isometric circuit traces and overhead/inter-pad power buses.
3. **Strict Right-Panel Discipline**: The `[912..1280]` panel contains **only** the 4 WarGames bars (`MONEY`, `WATER`, `OPINION`, `DEMAND`) and the single `WEEK 7 REQUEST` status box—never sparklines, sub-headers, or stacked button menus.
4. **Spatial & Conditional Controls**: Pad wireframes appear **only** on the hovered pad **only** while an install or silicon upgrade is valid; substation breakers appear **only** beside the substation **only** while halls are active.
5. **World Visibility on Terminal States**: `BLACKOUT` and `WEEK 7 SURVIVED` never obscure the miniature town behind a centered modal wall.

---

## 7. FAILURE
- **How Failure Approaches (Law 10 & Law 14)**: Pushing efficiency upgrades while holding `[1] SELL` drives `DEMAND` above `+82%` (crimson bar), dims house windows in staggered voltage-sag waves (`threshold 0.44..0.96`), pitches up the WebAudio 58Hz/116Hz substation hum, and triggers high-frequency brownout crackles (`>86%` capacity).
- **How Failure Lands**: Sustaining `loadMW > capMW * 1.03` for `0.70s` without buffered battery charge trips the main substation breaker—snapping all `63` house windows dark, showering sparks across the transformer yard, sweeping transformer pitch down (`155Hz → 24Hz`), and turning `WEEK 7 REQUEST` crimson (`GRID BLACKOUT` / `[R] REBUILD WEEK`).
- **Immediate Recovery (Law 8)**: Pressing `R`, `Enter`, `Space`, or clicking resets cleanly to Day 1 in `<16ms` with deterministic PRNG (`?seed=N`).

void_audit_sections.heading: A. Brutally Honest Before-Rebuild Critique (`pair_002`, `pair_005`, `pair_008` Before)
void_audit_sections.content:
Comparing the first-pass `projects/g18/m2/game/index.html` side-by-side against the Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash seed video (`video/gameplay.mp4` / `study/sheet.jpg`) exposed five severe visual and systemic failures:

1. **Ugly Pasted Chip Cutouts with Circular Blue Fog Halos (`pair_002/005/008` right vs. left)**:
   - In the Omni video (`f_001` → `f_014` → `f_033`), the 4 foreground brown dirt lots clear into flush, nocturnal dark-slate architectural server-hall / cryo-heatsink modules (`#1c2530` fin valleys, `#5e748b` matte gunmetal silicon dies) whose circuit traces ignite strictly along the isometric pad trenches in electric cyan (`#38d8ff`) and golden-amber (`#ffb830`).
   - The first-pass game extracted studio-lit `#e5ebf0` bright white-silver sprites from `server_hall_and_chip_icons.png` without nocturnal color grading and drew `ctx.ellipse` radial blue gradients (`rgba(80,205,255,0.65)`) beneath every pad—turning the 4 server halls into bright floating stickers inside giant circular blue soap bubbles, while unbuilt lots stamped permanent `+ CHIP LOT` text labels over visible cyan bleed from the raw map asset.
2. **Uncleaned 3-Strip Composite Artifacts & Frozen Ghost Steam in `town_map_with_lights_3_load_levels.png`**:
   - Because `town_map_with_lights_3_load_levels.png` (`1376×768`) was generated as 3 vertical load-level strips (`x≈341` and `x≈687`), its right strip baked a **permanent static white mushroom cloud of steam** above the cooling towers (`x=765..912, y=0..265`) and pre-baked glowing pads in the foreground. In `pair_002` (`t=2s`), the Omni video has **zero steam** on its matte dark cooling towers while load is calm (`+12%`), whereas the old game showed a huge frozen painted cloud with moving circles layered over it.
3. **Detached Toast Banner Violating Law 6 (`drawMapToast`)**:
   - A 590px yellow-bordered toast box (`CHIP INSTALLED: Query cost -$0.01 -> Orders accelerating!` / `JEVONS REBOUND...`) sat pinned across the top-left transmission corridor—narrating in prose what the world's surging cables, boiling cooling towers, and flickering house windows were supposed to show physically.
4. **Severe Right-Sidebar Clutter (`drawDashboard`)**:
   - `sheet.jpg` has an iconic, monumental WarGames right panel (`x=912..1280`): **only** the 4 bold monospace bars (`MONEY`, `WATER`, `OPINION`, `DEMAND`), generous dark `#0d1114` void, and the stark bordered `WEEK 7 REQUEST` box (`+1 hall: clear 4 lots` → two-tone amber/green `+1 hall: COMPLETE`).
   - The first-pass build crammed in a top `DAY X/7 · ... $0.019/q` micro-header, a `112px` `GRID LOAD` sparkline box in the middle void, and 2–3 stacked verbose instruction buttons (`[SPACE] INSTALL GEN-3 PHOTON DIE`, `[1] SELL CAPACITY +$$$ · Jevons surge!`, etc.) inside the `WEEK 7` box—shrinking and crowding every element.
5. **Turn-Locked Menu Play & Opaque End Modals**:
   - Every 1.05s the simulation froze into a sidebar button-clicking prompt instead of letting Jevons' paradox play out spatially on the isometric grid, and `BLACKOUT` slapped a `690×360` opaque modal over the map—hiding the darkened miniature town at the exact moment its blackout mattered most.

void_audit_sections.heading: B. Honest Post-Rebuild Assessment & Remaining Differences
void_audit_sections.content:
- **What Now Matches `sheet.jpg` & Exceeds First-Pass Playability**:
  - **Zero circular blue halos & nocturnal-graded flush modules**: Sprites extracted from `server_hall_and_chip_icons.png` are pixel-graded from `#d8d8d8` studio lighting down to nocturnal gunmetal slate (`#5e748b` / `#17212b`), seated on flush stepped isometric plinths, with 24 crisp isometric circuit conduits per pad pulsing in cyan (`#38d8ff`) and amber (`#ffb830`) strictly inside the pad geometry.
  - **Clean nocturnal base map & true zero-to-billowing steam**: Baked ghost steam above the hyperbolic cooling towers (`y < 263`), vertical strip dividers, and pre-baked foreground pad bleed are scrubbed offscreen; cooling towers stand crisp and silent at `t=0..2s` and billow volumetric steam only as halls boil cooling water.
  - **Stark `sheet.jpg` right panel**: Top micro-header, middle sparkline box, toast banner, and stacked sidebar buttons are 100% cut. Only `MONEY`, `WATER`, `OPINION`, `DEMAND`, and the exact `WEEK 7 REQUEST` box remain.
  - **Spatial Law-5 controls**: Clicking the 4 dirt lots / halls installs & upgrades dies directly in-world; 3 compact diegetic substation breaker switches (`[1] SELL`, `[2] BUFFER`, `[3] CAP`) sit right beside the substation transformers (`x=768, y=548..644`) with a live power filament routing into the Hall Bus, Battery Racks, or Town Limiter.
- **Remaining Honest Differences vs. Seed Video**:
  1. **Diegetic Substation Breaker Rack (`x=768..896, y=548..644`)**: The passive Omni video has no allocation switches visible because the video viewer cannot toggle `[1] SELL / [2] BUFFER / [3] CAP`; we place a compact 3-throw breaker unit in the empty lower-right substation corner (dormant at `t=0` when `0` halls are built, armed once compute is online) so the core verb (`Allocate: sell, save or cap`) is playable spatially without polluting the right panel.
  2. **Pad Drop-In Trajectory**: In `f_009`–`f_014` of the Omni video, Omni briefly hallucinates an upper-row chip silhouette translating across the town edge before settling onto the 4 foreground lots; in our playable build, clicking each of the 4 brown dirt lots drops its module cleanly (`32px` vertical cubic ease-out latch) onto that exact lot's coordinates so spatial mouse picking is 1:1 deterministic.
  3. **Procedural Canvas Plasma vs. Diffusion Lightning**: Our surging golden transmission filaments and pad-to-pad arcs use multi-strand procedural jittered polylines (`#ffb830` outer glow + `#fff4c8` core) rather than neural video diffusion blur, trading painterly softness for 60 fps real-time responsiveness to player breaker throws.

# VOIDBASTARD-TAO AUDIT · `g24` — Memory Munitions (M2)

## 0. HONEST VIDEO-VS-GAME CRITIQUE & GEMINI PROVENANCE

### Honest Critique of the First-Pass Build vs. Omni Seed Video (`study/sheet.jpg`)
Comparing `video/gameplay.mp4` (`study/sheet.jpg`, `study/f_005.jpg`, `f_014.jpg`, `f_022.jpg`, `f_036.jpg`) directly against the original M2 HTML build (`pairs/pair_002.00.jpg`, `pair_005.00.jpg`, `pair_008.00.jpg`) exposed five glaring regressions:

1. **Three Detached HUD Boxes Violating the Pure Open Sky**: The Omni seed video has **zero** top HUD bars—its entire emotional punch comes from warm sepia photographs floating starkly against deep void black (`#05080a`) above a glowing mint grid. The first-pass HTML build bolted three boxed monospace banners across the top edge (`CHASSIS 68% | MODE: [K] DISABLE BEAM`, `MEMORY #1 SHATTERED: GABLE HOUSE, 1984 / Minigun tore this memory into unreadable shards.`, and `SAVED 0/8 · ERASED 1/8`), plus floating rectangular enemy health bars and a literal `"✓ SAVED TO ALBUM"` text label hovering over recovered photographs.
2. **Dwarfed Actor Scale & Flat Lighting**: In `study/f_005.jpg` and `f_022.jpg`, the cyber-soldier (~395px tall, 55% of viewport height) and magenta sentinel (~415px tall, 58% of viewport height) command the frame with glossy cyan/magenta floor light pools. The first-pass HTML build rendered the soldier at 248px (34% height) and enemies at 265–272px, leaving the characters tiny and flat.
3. **Zoomed-In Muddy Shards Instead of Miniature Photographs**: In `study/f_014.jpg` and `f_022.jpg`, a shattered robot erupts into dozens of crisp miniature golden-bordered Polaroids tumbling in 3D perspective and settling foreshortened onto the glossy grid floor. The first-pass build sliced a 240×180 canvas into 30 zoomed-in UV sub-rectangles that clumped in a blurry beige cloud behind the player.
4. **Leftover Enclosed Studio-Grey Cutout Islands**: Inspection of `player_robot_with_minigun.png` and `2_enemy_robot_types.png` revealed `1,775` and `6,805` residual studio-grey (`~#cfcfcf–#d8d8d8`) pixels trapped inside arm/rifle/leg loops where edge flood-fill could not reach, plus grey fringe spill.
5. **2.5-Second Pre-Roll Desync in Verification Capture**: Because `?autostart` immediately activated enemy movement during `record_play.mjs`'s 2.5s pre-screencast warmup, Enemy #0 was already dead before `t = 2.0s`, causing `pair_002`, `pair_005`, and `pair_008` to miss the Omni video's choreography and overlap disabled robots behind the player's legs.

### What Was Rebuilt & What Honestly Still Differs from the Omni Video
- **What we fixed**: Stripped 100% of top HUD boxes, toast banners, floating enemy health bars, and `"✓ SAVED TO ALBUM"` text; scrubbed enclosed studio-grey pockets and edge fringes on both sprite sheets; scaled the soldier (`374px`) and sentinels (`402px`) to match the video's arcade framing; added additive cyan/magenta/gold floor light pools, two-pass neon grid bloom, 3D-tilting miniature Polaroid shards that settle foreshortened onto the floor, kneeling powered-down robot clipping with shoulder steam (`f_036.jpg`), and diegetic spine-cell health + muzzle barrel heat + core harmonic lock rings.
- **What honestly still differs from `gameplay.mp4`**:
  - **2D Sprite Poses vs. Continuous 3D Mesh Articulation**: The Omni 1.2 Flash video renders continuous 3D skeletal articulation, smooth torso twist while running, and volumetric raytraced specular reflections on metallic armor plates. Our HTML5 Canvas game animates discrete 2D sprite frames from `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` (`player_robot_with_minigun.png` and `2_enemy_robot_types.png`), which carry bold 2D inked outlines rather than smooth PBR shading.
  - **Procedural Particle Physics vs. Neural Fluid Simulation**: Our shattering Polaroids, golden bokeh fireflies, and 4-strand sine-wave plasma beam approximate the Omni video's neural slow-motion curl and volumetric smoke in real-time 60fps 2D Canvas, rather than per-pixel 3D depth-of-field blur.

### Complete Gemini API & Asset Provenance (`gemini_log.json`)
- **Seed Gameplay Video (`video/gameplay.mp4`)**
  - **Model**: `gemini-omni-1.2-flash`
  - **Interaction ID**: `v1_ChdETUw5YXBhT0JvbU95dE1QcjlLRXVBdxIXRE1MOWFwYU9Cb21PeXRNUHI5S0V1QXc`
  - **Timestamp / Elapsed**: `2026-11-18T15:19:42Z` · `44.38s` (`1280x720`, `24.0 fps`, `10.027s`, 40 study frames `f_001.jpg`–`f_040.jpg`)
  - **Reference Input**: `projects/g24/m2/refs/m2_main_ref.png`
  - **Prompt**: *"1980s arcade neon side-scrolling run-and-gun game on deep void black (#07060c) with electric mint (#5dff9e) vector grid floors and hot magenta (#ff4fb0) robot enemies. Steady side-on 2.5D tracking camera. A sleek cybernetic soldier fires rapid neon bursts, then switches to a precision disable beam: the first robot shatters into warm golden-sepia photographic memory shards floating in slow motion, while the second robot powers down intact releasing a glowing intact memory photograph. Continuous unbroken gameplay shot, no scene cuts, no HUD text. Use the reference image for perspective grid and neon palette. Sound design: punchy 80s synth bassline, laser zaps, crystalline chime. No dialogue."*
- **Generated Visual & Audio Assets (`assets/gemini_log.json`)**
  1. `player_robot_with_minigun.png` — `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` (`17.11s`, `1:1` 1K, cutout cleaned from `_raw.png`), grounded on `study/f_014.jpg` & `study/f_027.jpg` (`id: v1_ChdFTUw5YXYtMU12UG55dE1QMnRUNW1BMBIXRU1MOWF2LTFNdlBueXRNUDJ0VDVtQTA`).
  2. `2_enemy_robot_types.png` — `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` (`20.16s`, `1:1` 1K, cutout cleaned from `_raw.png`), grounded on `study/f_014.jpg` & `study/f_027.jpg` (`id: v1_ChdJY0w5YXNTRU5zeXR3YlVQcDVIMnlBaxIXSWNMOWFzU0VOc3l0d2JVUHA1SDJ5QWs`).
  3. `8_memory_fragments_photo_map_message.png` — `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` (`20.72s`, `16:9` 1K), grounded on `study/f_014.jpg` & `study/f_027.jpg` (`id: v1_ChdPTUw5YXZyZUpfT0N5dE1QMjh5VHVBZxIXT01MOWF2cmVKX09DeXRNUDI4eVR1QWc`).
  4. `bgm_loop.mp3` — `lyria-3-clip-preview` (`14.12s`, 30s instrumental synth loop), grounded on `study/f_014.jpg` (`id: v1_ChdTc0w5YXJTWkxQek15dE1QM3Q3ci1BURIXU3NMOWFyU1pMUHpNeXRNUDN0N3ItQVE`).

## 1. WAY
Speed erases evidence; restraint preserves identity. Every robot on the neon grid carries one irreplaceable human memory inside its core: pulling the minigun trigger (`Space`/`J`) clears the threat fast in a visceral burst of unreachable golden shards, whereas holding the closer-range precision disable beam (`K`/`Shift`) forces the player to stand exposed in the line of fire until the robot kneels and surrenders the photograph whole.

---

## 2. OBSTRUCTION
- **Detached Top Telemetry Chrome**: Three boxed top banners (`CHASSIS %`, `MEMORY SHATTERED/RECOVERED` toast, `SAVED/ERASED` counter) dragged the player's eyes out of the gunfight and ruined the stark black void above the grid.
- **Floating Health Bars & Text Tags**: Rectangular HP bars over enemies and `"✓ SAVED TO ALBUM"` floating strings turned poetic visual consequences into spreadsheet rows.
- **Boxed Modal Title Wall**: A 900×440 bordered instruction box hid the live neon world on startup.

---

## 3. KEEP-CUT LEDGER

| Surface / Element | Verdict | Reason (VOIDBASTARD-TAO Element Test) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Top-left `CHASSIS %` + weapon mode box + 8-pip bar | **CUT** | Replaced by 4 diegetic cyan/magenta spine cells & armor rim-glow on the cyber-soldier + live barrel heat glow on the gun tip. |
| Top-center `MEMORY #N SHATTERED / RECOVERED` toast box | **CUT** | Redundant narration of what the player already sees happening physically in the center of the world. |
| Top-right `SAVED X/8 · ERASED Y/8` counter box | **CUT** | Deferred to the end-of-run physical `ALBUM` table (`COMPLETE`), keeping active combat 100% chrome-free. |
| Floating rectangular HP/disable bar over enemy heads | **CUT** | Replaced by golden memory-fissures leaking from damaged robot cores and a constricting cyan harmonic ring directly on the chest core during beam lock. |
| `"✓ SAVED TO ALBUM"` text above recovered Polaroid | **CUT** | Replaced by physical absorption of warm golden fireflies into the soldier's visor as you walk past (`+12` integrity). |
| Boxed 900×440 Title Modal (`strokeRect`) | **CUT** | Replaced in non-autostart `REST` by open live world + spatial `[SPACE] SHATTER` / `[K] RECOVER` callouts beside the muzzle. |
| Twin-helix cyan beam + 3D sepia shards + kneeling steam | **KEEP & UPGRADE** | Core spatial truth of the two verbs and direct visual anchor to `study/sheet.jpg`. |
| End-of-level 8-slot Memory Album + `[R]` recovery | **KEEP & REFINE** | Essential `COMPLETE` / `RECOVERY` payoff showing kept Polaroids vs. torn shards without modal bloat. |

---

## 4. STATE MAP

| State | Dominant Purpose & Action | What Is Shown (Spatial / Diegetic) | What Is Hidden |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `REST` | Commit first movement or shot (non-autostart) | Live neon grid, breathing soldier, title mark in upper void, `[SPACE] SHATTER` / `[K] RECOVER` beside gun barrel | All top bars, album grid, enemy fire |
| `READY` | Poised entry on `?autostart` before first input | Pure chrome-free neon grid, cyber-soldier at `x=295`, Sentinel #0 poised on right, zero text | Title text, HUD boxes, premature ambush |
| `WORKING` | Run, jump, shatter (`Space`/`J`), or lock beam (`K`/`Shift`) | Spine integrity cells, muzzle heat glow, plasma bolts, golden core fissures, cyan core lock ring | All text chrome and banners |
| `CHANGED` | Witness irreversible memory erasure or intact recovery | 38 slow-mo 3D-tumbling sepia Polaroids settling on floor OR kneeling robot venting teal steam beside a firefly-haloed Polaroid | Modal popups, toast banners |
| `COMPLETE` | Inspect the story pieced together from kept vs. erased memories | 8 physical Polaroids/maps/letters laid out on dark void (`KEPT X/8 · SHATTERED Y/8`) + `[R] RUN AGAIN` | Combat actors |
| `FAULT` | Recognize chassis failure on the grid | Soldier dropped to one knee on the neon grid with dimmed visor + spatial `[R] REBOOT CHASSIS` beside chassis | Full-screen boxed game-over modal |
| `RECOVERY` | Instant deterministic reset (`[R]` / `Enter` / click) | Immediate transition back into `WORKING` at `x=295` with fresh chassis and reset seed | Loading screens or confirmation prompts |

---

## 5. WIREFRAMES

```text
[WORKING / CHANGED — ZERO HUD CHROME, 100% OPEN CENTER]
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                          |
|          [ ~ ~ drifting miniature sepia Polaroids ~ ~ ]                  |
|                                               .  *  +---------+  *  .    |
|                 (4 spine cells)              *      |  WARM   |      *   |
|                    [Soldier]====(cyan helix)=======>|  SEPIA  |  (steam) |
|                    /      \                         |  PHOTO  |   [Robot]|
|~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~/~~~~~~~~\~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~+---------+~~~/~~~~\~|
|  \      \      \  (cyan pool)   \      \     (gold pool)    (magenta)    |
+---\------\------\----------------\------\-----------------------\--------+

[FAULT / RECOVERY]                        [COMPLETE — PHYSICAL ALBUM]
+------------------------------------+    +------------------------------------+
|                                    |    |     KEPT 4/8  ·  SHATTERED 4/8     |
|                                    |    |  [Photo 1] [Torn #2] [Photo 3] ... |
|      [Kneeling Soldier] [R] REBOOT |    |  [Torn #5] [Map #6 ] [Note #7] ... |
|~~~~~~/~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~|    |            [R] RUN AGAIN           |
+------------------------------------+    +------------------------------------+
```

---

## 6. VOID CONTRACT
1. **Zero Top-Edge or Corner HUD Chrome**: During `READY`, `WORKING`, and `CHANGED`, zero pixels in the upper sky (`y < 180`) are occupied by UI panels, counters, or text banners; only world-space sepia shards and golden embers may traverse the void.
2. **Every Consequence Is Physical and Non-Blocking**: Destroying or disabling a robot never pauses player movement or spawns a text modal; shattered memories scatter onto the reflective grid floor, and recovered Polaroids hover in world space with their sepia title inked onto the paper border itself.
3. **Controls & Telemetry Live on the Hardware**: Integrity lives on the soldier's 4 spine cells + armor rim hue; weapon stress lives on muzzle heat bloom; disable progress lives as a constricting cyan ring on the target robot's chest core.

---

## 7. FAILURE
- **Failure Mode Prevented #1 (Accidental First-Click Shot / Pre-Roll Desync)**: Previously, `?autostart` ran enemies during headless browser warmup so Enemy #0 died off-beat. Gating enemy advance on `READY -> WORKING` engagement makes human iframe focus and automated capture align cleanly at `t = 0.0s`.
- **Failure Mode Prevented #2 (Minigun Trivializing Disable Risk)**: Added barrel heat buildup (`p.heat` -> `0.55s` steam vent overheat) and `+12` chassis integrity restoration when passing a recovered Polaroid, rewarding players mechanically as well as narratively for daring to use the close-range disable beam.
- **Failure Mode Prevented #3 (Opaque Studio Grey Loops)**: Scrubbed enclosed neutral studio-grey islands (`#cfcfcf–#d8d8d8`) both in the saved PNG assets and via an offscreen canvas pass on load.

---

  - `projects/g24/m2/game/play.mjs` (responsive keyboard playtest showcasing mid-air minigun duel at `2.0s`, drifting golden shards at `5.0s`, and intact Polaroid recovery beside the kneeling robot at `8.0s`).
- **Verification Metrics (`run_pipeline.py --project g24 --milestone m2 --stages verify`)**:

void_audit_sections.heading: 6. VOID CONTRACT
void_audit_sections.content:
1. **Zero Top-Edge or Corner HUD Chrome**: During `READY`, `WORKING`, and `CHANGED`, zero pixels in the upper sky (`y < 180`) are occupied by UI panels, counters, or text banners; only world-space sepia shards and golden embers may traverse the void.
2. **Every Consequence Is Physical and Non-Blocking**: Destroying or disabling a robot never pauses player movement or spawns a text modal; shattered memories scatter onto the reflective grid floor, and recovered Polaroids hover in world space with their sepia title inked onto the paper border itself.
3. **Controls & Telemetry Live on the Hardware**: Integrity lives on the soldier's 4 spine cells + armor rim hue; weapon stress lives on muzzle heat bloom; disable progress lives as a constricting cyan ring on the target robot's chest core.

void_audit_sections.heading: 7. FAILURE
void_audit_sections.content:
- **Failure Mode Prevented #1 (Accidental First-Click Shot / Pre-Roll Desync)**: Previously, `?autostart` ran enemies during headless browser warmup so Enemy #0 died off-beat. Gating enemy advance on `READY -> WORKING` engagement makes human iframe focus and automated capture align cleanly at `t = 0.0s`.
- **Failure Mode Prevented #2 (Minigun Trivializing Disable Risk)**: Added barrel heat buildup (`p.heat` -> `0.55s` steam vent overheat) and `+12` chassis integrity restoration when passing a recovered Polaroid, rewarding players mechanically as well as narratively for daring to use the close-range disable beam.
- **Failure Mode Prevented #3 (Opaque Studio Grey Loops)**: Scrubbed enclosed neutral studio-grey islands (`#cfcfcf–#d8d8d8`) both in the saved PNG assets and via an offscreen canvas pass on load.

# VOID_AUDIT — Group 8: That One Team (M2)

**Engine**: VOIDBASTARD-TAO (Operational Emptiness Engine)  
**Scope**: `projects/g8/m2/`  
**Verification**: `824 frames, 13.9 s, 59.3 fps, 0 console errors` (`best_window`: `1.00 s -> 9.00 s`, score `0.0196`)

---

## 0. HONEST VIDEO-VS-GAME CRITIQUE & GEMINI PROVENANCE

### A. Brutally Honest Critique of the Prior M2 Build vs. `study/sheet.jpg`
Inspecting the prior M2 HTML5 build (`pairs/pair_002.00.jpg`, `pair_005.00.jpg`, `pair_008.00.jpg`) against the Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash seed clip (`video/gameplay.mp4` / `study/sheet.jpg`) exposed five severe failures:

1. **Detached & Colliding Text Clutter (Violated Laws 1, 2, 3, 5, 6)**:
   - Top-right bureaucratic labels (`SECTOR 01 · FULLGRANT / ALL MOVEMENT SYSTEMS ONLINE`, `SECTOR 02 · HEAVIER AIR / GLIDE OFFLINE — RELY ON DASH, DOUBLE JUMP & WALL KICK`) were absent from the video and physically collided right across the `GLIDE` HUD box in `pair_005.00.jpg` and `pair_008.00.jpg`.
   - Crossing a threshold arch spawned a heavy `660×66` bottom-center text modal (`GLIDE REVOKED — AIRFOIL PRIVILEGE RECLAIMED`) and froze progression for `1.05s`, whereas `sheet.jpg` (`f_019..f_025`) communicates ability loss purely through the arch's radial golden detonation, aura detachment, glyph fracture, and real-time world desaturation.
   - Room resets slapped a full-screen `ROOM RESET` black modal over the canvas, and `title` stacked four lines of instructional copy across the center.
2. **Unclean Sprite Alpha Cutouts & Studio-Grey Pockets**:
   - Pixel inspection of the prior cutouts on `#14121c` dark sky revealed exterior flood-fill had missed enclosed `#cccccc`–`#d3d3d3` studio-grey pockets and anti-aliased edge fringes:
     - `player_sprite_with_ability_states.png`: `1,115` opaque studio-grey pixels + `4,547` semi-grey fringe pixels, purple-blended bright slits trapped under the armpits/legs in rows 3–4, and a hard opaque cream sticker rim around rows 1–2.
     - `sound_set_that_thins_out.png`: `5,844` opaque `#d1d1d1` studio pixels trapped inside the concentric golden and violet hologram rings atop Speakers 1 & 2 (visibly glowing as a grey blob behind the player in old `pair_005.00.jpg`), plus grey box fringes around the tiny floating pixels above Speakers 3–5.
     - `tile_set_colour_and_greyscale_versions.png`: `26,077` opaque studio-grey pixels trapped inside chain-link loops and rubble gaps, plus pale white sparkle halos around Row-1 diamond crystals (`y=37`).
3. **Repetitive Checkerboard Tile Wallpaper vs. Sculpted Architecture**:
   - Large cliffs repeated `darkFill` in a visible `64×64` purple square grid, and floating islands repeated `island2` jagged bottoms four times side-by-side instead of sculpting tapered stalactite underbellies (`f_005.jpg`, `f_014.jpg`) and seamless weathered ashlar stone courses (`f_027.jpg`).
4. **Disconnected Scene Cuts, Flat Zoom, & Broken `t=8.00s` Pacing**:
   - The prior build split the game into five teleporting level cuts with a static `camY` and tiny `~78px` runner. By `t=8.00s` (`pair_008.00.jpg`), the Omni video had already detonated the arch, vanished the HUD, and transitioned into a haunting monochrome stone run, while the old game was still stuck in purple Sector 2.
5. **Shallow Audio Subtraction**:
   - Only `bgm.volume` stepped down; `bgm_loop.mp3` lacked frequency filtering and lacked the prompt's layer-by-layer synth arpeggio stem subtraction.

### B. What Was Rebuilt & Fixed
- **VFX Color-Unmixed Alpha Cleaning**: Re-derived `player_sprite_with_ability_states.png`, `tile_set_colour_and_greyscale_versions.png`, and `sound_set_that_thins_out.png` from `*_raw.png` using connected-component studio-pocket detection, boundary foreground unmixing (`C = αF + (1−α)BG`), armpit-slit clearing, and soft golden rim falloff; switched crystal pickups to the crisp black-outlined Row-2 sprites (`y=115`).
- **Continuous Unbroken Architectural World (`WORLD_W = 4920`, `ZOOM = 1.22`)**: Rebuilt all five levels as five contiguous sectors in a single unbroken camera shot separated by monumental Threshold Arches (`x = 2020, 2630, 3220, 3780`) and a final silent stone doorway (`x = 4680`), with sculpted stalactite islands, a towering vertical violet monolith column, and seamless weathered ashlar stone slabs in monochrome.
- **Pure Top-Left Fracturing Glyphs**: Cut all sector titles, subtitles, bottom revoke cards, and reset banners. Only `DASH`, `DOUBLE`, `WALL`, `GLIDE` remain at top-left; each physically cracks, crosses out, and bursts 24 tumbling screen-space shards when surrendered, then dissolves completely (`alpha -> 0`) upon entering the monochrome `LAST WALK` (`pair_008.00.jpg`).
- **Celeste-Grade Movement & Multi-Layer Audio Subtraction**: Added `0.12s` coyote time, `0.12s` jump buffering, variable jump cut, apex hang-time boost, corner-nudge forgiveness, spring squash/stretch, hit-stop micro-freezes, golden crescent dash auras, concentric violet double-jump shockwaves, WebAudio Biquad low-pass filtering on `../assets/bgm_loop.mp3` (`18 kHz -> 4.6 kHz -> 1.75 kHz -> 620 Hz -> silent`), and a 4-stem D-minor synth arpeggio whose instruments drop out one-by-one as each ability is surrendered.

### C. Honest Accounting of Remaining Video-vs-Game Differences
We refuse to claim fake "identical" perfection between a generative video model and a real-time 2D HTML5 game:
1. **Neural Fluid VFX vs. Real-Time Canvas2D Primitives**: `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` paints per-frame volumetric portal rays, organic plasma dash ribbons, and painterly lighting transitions across surfaces. Our 60fps Canvas2D renderer approximates these honestly with radial gradients, rotating crescent arcs, tapered polyline ribbons, and discrete sprite frames.
2. **Prompt-Hallucinated `#14121c` Text in Video vs. True `DASH` Glyph**: In `study/sheet.jpg` (`f_001..f_020`), Omni 1.2 Flash leaked the literal background hex code `#14121c` from its prompt into the leftmost HUD box instead of `DASH` (from `refs/m2_main_ref.png`). Following VOIDBASTARD-TAO Law 14, our game displays the true operable glyph `DASH`.
3. **Four Playable Subtraction Arches vs. Single Video Transition**: The 10s seed video compresses the concept into one dramatic arch transition (`t ≈ 5.0s`) from vivid movement directly to monochrome stone. Because `spec.json` mandates surrendering four distinct abilities (`GLIDE`, `WALL`, `DOUBLE`, `DASH`) across five playable stages before `LAST WALK`, our continuous world includes three compact mid-run subtraction sectors (`Sectors 1–3`, `t ≈ 5.1s..7.6s`) featuring diegetic `sound_set_that_thins_out.png` monoliths before emerging into pure HUD-free monochrome by `t = 8.0s`.

## 1. WAY
*That One Team* is an operational poem of subtraction: the player begins in radiant gold and violet possessing every movement verb (`DASH`, `DOUBLE`, `WALL`, `GLIDE`) and surrenders them one by one through monumental Threshold Arches until colour, music, jumping, and the HUD itself vanish—leaving only a quiet, grounded walk across dark stone to a silent doorway. Every pixel and audio stem must physically embody what still remains right now, and nothing more.

---

## 2. OBSTRUCTION
The prior interface distrusted its own world:
- It narrated subtraction in prose (`SECTOR 02 · HEAVIER AIR`, `GLIDE OFFLINE — RELY ON...`, `GLIDE REVOKED — AIRFOIL PRIVILEGE RECLAIMED`) instead of letting the player *feel* heavier gravity, *hear* the upper bell stem vanish, and *watch* the glyph fracture and saturation drain.
- It broke spatial continuity with hard scene cuts and full-screen `ROOM RESET` modals that stole focus from the runner's body.
- Leftover `#d8d8d8` studio-grey pockets inside sprites betrayed the illusion of a deep `#14121c` void.

---

## 3. KEEP-CUT LEDGER

| Surface / Element | Verdict | VOIDBASTARD-TAO Law & Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Top-left 4 Ability Glyphs (`DASH`, `DOUBLE`, `WALL`, `GLIDE`) | **KEEP & FRACTURE** | Laws 2, 4, 6, 11: Shows exact remaining movement capabilities; cracks, crosses out, bursts shards on loss, and dissolves to `0` opacity when all abilities are gone. |
| Top-right `SECTOR 0X` title & offline instruction subtitle | **CUT** | Laws 1, 2, 6: Pure bureaucratic narration that collided with the `GLIDE` glyph box; world saturation and architecture already show sector progression. |
| Bottom `660×66` `ABILITY REVOKED` banner card | **CUT** | Laws 3, 6, 11: Replaced by in-world golden shockwave sphere, rising detached ability orb, hit-stop, stem drop, and physical glyph fracture. |
| Full-screen `ROOM RESET` black text overlay | **CUT** | Laws 6, 8, 11: Replaced by immediate particle shatter & reform at the active sector's Threshold Arch checkpoint. |
| Multi-line `TITLE` keybinding paragraph & dark veil | **CUT** | Laws 1, 3, 5: Replaced by live breathing world, open `THAT ONE TEAM` header, and a spatial `[SPACE]` cue directly above the runner. |
| End-screen verbose paragraph (`NOTHING LEFT TO TAKE...`) | **CUT** | Law 12 (Completion creates no new demand) & Law 8: Runner sits quietly at the final doorway (`monoSit1 -> monoSit2`); after stillness settles, a dim spatial `[R]` appears above the runner. |
| `[P]` / `[Esc]` Pause & `[R]` Checkpoint/Full Retry | **KEEP (CONDITIONAL)** | Laws 4, 7, 8, 14: Invisible during active flow; `[P]` exposes clean `[P] RESUME  [R] RETRY` only while paused. |
| Diegetic Sound Monoliths (`sound_set_that_thins_out.png`) | **KEEP (CLEANED)** | Law 6: World-anchored towers physically lose their golden/violet holographic rings alongside the WebAudio stem & low-pass subtraction. |
| Scanline white-stripe overlay | **CUT** | Law 13: Added muddiness over monochrome stone; kept only clean radial vignette matching `sheet.jpg`. |

---

## 4. STATE MAP

| **READY** | `lvl` (grounded at sector start / ledge) | Read upcoming gap/wall/spikes against active top-left glyphs; initiate run, jump, or dash. | Crisp active glyphs lit `#f2f2f2`; surrendered glyphs scarred & dimmed; world saturation & music stems match current sector (`1.00`, `0.68`, `0.36`, `0.12`). |
| **WORKING** | `lvl` (airborne / dashing / wall-sliding / gliding) & `walk` | Chain valid movement verbs across void gaps (`lvl`), or walk steadily across monochrome stone (`walk`). `[P]` pauses; `[R]` retries. | Golden crescent dash aura, violet double-jump rings, wall-slide sparks, or billowing monochrome stone dust + lonely footsteps (`walk`, HUD dissolved to `0`). |
| **CHANGED** | `take` (crossing Threshold Arch `0..3`) | Witness irreversible surrender of one ability while momentum carries runner smoothly through the arch. | `32ms` hit-stop -> `0.55x` slow-mo glide; radial golden sphere; detached orb rises to keystone; glyph cracks & sheds 24 shards; saturation & BGM filter step down; 1 synth stem mutes. |

## 5. WIREFRAMES

## 6. VOID CONTRACT
1. **Center & Sky Sovereignty**: Never place persistent text banners, sector titles, score counters, or modal dialogs anywhere in the sky or center viewport.
2. **Four Glyphs -> Zero Glyphs**: Top-left holds at most four ability glyphs (`DASH`, `DOUBLE`, `WALL`, `GLIDE`). void_audit_sections.heading: A. Brutally Honest Critique of the Prior M2 Build vs. `study/sheet.jpg`
void_audit_sections.content:
Inspecting the prior M2 HTML5 build (`pairs/pair_002.00.jpg`, `pair_005.00.jpg`, `pair_008.00.jpg`) against the Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash seed clip (`video/gameplay.mp4` / `study/sheet.jpg`) exposed five severe failures:

1. **Detached & Colliding Text Clutter (Violated Laws 1, 2, 3, 5, 6)**:
   - Top-right bureaucratic labels (`SECTOR 01 · FULLGRANT / ALL MOVEMENT SYSTEMS ONLINE`, `SECTOR 02 · HEAVIER AIR / GLIDE OFFLINE — RELY ON DASH, DOUBLE JUMP & WALL KICK`) were absent from the video and physically collided right across the `GLIDE` HUD box in `pair_005.00.jpg` and `pair_008.00.jpg`.
   - Crossing a threshold arch spawned a heavy `660×66` bottom-center text modal (`GLIDE REVOKED — AIRFOIL PRIVILEGE RECLAIMED`) and froze progression for `1.05s`, whereas `sheet.jpg` (`f_019..f_025`) communicates ability loss purely through the arch's radial golden detonation, aura detachment, glyph fracture, and real-time world desaturation.
   - Room resets slapped a full-screen `ROOM RESET` black modal over the canvas, and `title` stacked four lines of instructional copy across the center.
2. **Unclean Sprite Alpha Cutouts & Studio-Grey Pockets**:
   - Pixel inspection of the prior cutouts on `#14121c` dark sky revealed exterior flood-fill had missed enclosed `#cccccc`–`#d3d3d3` studio-grey pockets and anti-aliased edge fringes:
     - `player_sprite_with_ability_states.png`: `1,115` opaque studio-grey pixels + `4,547` semi-grey fringe pixels, purple-blended bright slits trapped under the armpits/legs in rows 3–4, and a hard opaque cream sticker rim around rows 1–2.
     - `sound_set_that_thins_out.png`: `5,844` opaque `#d1d1d1` studio pixels trapped inside the concentric golden and violet hologram rings atop Speakers 1 & 2 (visibly glowing as a grey blob behind the player in old `pair_005.00.jpg`), plus grey box fringes around the tiny floating pixels above Speakers 3–5.
     - `tile_set_colour_and_greyscale_versions.png`: `26,077` opaque studio-grey pixels trapped inside chain-link loops and rubble gaps, plus pale white sparkle halos around Row-1 diamond crystals (`y=37`).
3. **Repetitive Checkerboard Tile Wallpaper vs. Sculpted Architecture**:
   - Large cliffs repeated `darkFill` in a visible `64×64` purple square grid, and floating islands repeated `island2` jagged bottoms four times side-by-side instead of sculpting tapered stalactite underbellies (`f_005.jpg`, `f_014.jpg`) and seamless weathered ashlar stone courses (`f_027.jpg`).
4. **Disconnected Scene Cuts, Flat Zoom, & Broken `t=8.00s` Pacing**:
   - The prior build split the game into five teleporting level cuts with a static `camY` and tiny `~78px` runner. By `t=8.00s` (`pair_008.00.jpg`), the Omni video had already detonated the arch, vanished the HUD, and transitioned into a haunting monochrome stone run, while the old game was still stuck in purple Sector 2.
5. **Shallow Audio Subtraction**:
   - Only `bgm.volume` stepped down; `bgm_loop.mp3` lacked frequency filtering and lacked the prompt's layer-by-layer synth arpeggio stem subtraction.

void_audit_sections.content:

- **Continuous Unbroken Architectural World (`WORLD_W = 4920`, `ZOOM = 1.22`)**: Rebuilt all five levels as five contiguous sectors in a single unbroken camera shot separated by monumental Threshold Arches (`x = 2020, 2630, 3220, 3780`) and a final silent stone doorway (`x = 4680`), with sculpted stalactite islands, a towering vertical violet monolith column, and seamless weathered ashlar stone slabs in monochrome.

Only `DASH`, `DOUBLE`, `WALL`, `GLIDE` remain at top-left; each physically cracks, crosses out, and bursts 24 tumbling screen-space shards when surrendered, then dissolves completely (`alpha -> 0`) upon entering the monochrome `LAST WALK` (`pair_008.00.jpg`).

void_audit_sections.heading: C. Honest Accounting of Remaining Video-vs-Game Differences
void_audit_sections.content:
We refuse to claim fake "identical" perfection between a generative video model and a real-time 2D HTML5 game:
1. **Neural Fluid VFX vs. Real-Time Canvas2D Primitives**: `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` paints per-frame volumetric portal rays, organic plasma dash ribbons, and painterly lighting transitions across surfaces. Our 60fps Canvas2D renderer approximates these honestly with radial gradients, rotating crescent arcs, tapered polyline ribbons, and discrete sprite frames.
2. **Prompt-Hallucinated `#14121c` Text in Video vs. True `DASH` Glyph**: In `study/sheet.jpg` (`f_001..f_020`), Omni 1.2 Flash leaked the literal background hex code `#14121c` from its prompt into the leftmost HUD box instead of `DASH` (from `refs/m2_main_ref.png`). Following VOIDBASTARD-TAO Law 14, our game displays the true operable glyph `DASH`.
3. **Four Playable Subtraction Arches vs. Single Video Transition**: The 10s seed video compresses the concept into one dramatic arch transition (`t ≈ 5.0s`) from vivid movement directly to monochrome stone. Because `spec.json` mandates surrendering four distinct abilities (`GLIDE`, `WALL`, `DOUBLE`, `DASH`) across five playable stages before `LAST WALK`, our continuous world includes three compact mid-run subtraction sectors (`Sectors 1–3`, `t ≈ 5.1s..7.6s`) featuring diegetic `sound_set_that_thins_out.png` monoliths before emerging into pure HUD-free monochrome by `t = 8.0s`.
